chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab (Rabab), from Abu 'Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily, in Hell there is a valley called Ghassaq, in which are three hundred and thirty castles. In each castle are three hundred and thirty chambers. In each chamber are three hundred and thirty scorpions. In the stinger of each scorpion are three hundred and thirty sacs of venom. If a single one of those scorpions were to spray its venom on the people of Hell, it would cover them all with venom.
ai.seo_question: What is the valley of Ghassaq in Hell according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) in *Kitab al-Zuhd* employs the Shia literary device of *tabyin* (clarification) to illustrate the vastness of divine punishment through precise numerical gradation (300+300+300). It highlights the physical reality of Hell's topography, specifically the valley of Ghassaq, serving as a vivid reminder of the consequences of sin in Shia eschatological tradition.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 5.Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abū ʿUbaydah, from Abū Jaʿfar (a) who said, “

Verily there is a valley in Hell which is called Ghassāq. In it are three hundred and thirty castles. Each castle has three hundred and thirty chambers and in each chamber, there are three hundred and thirty scorpions. Inside the stinger of each of these scorpions there are thirty-three sacs of venom. If a single one of those scorpions were to spray its venom on the inmates of Hell, it would [suffice to] cover them [all] with venom.”
